paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches me. You can hear God say no, and still go looking for a yes. God told Balaam plainly, "Do not go with them. You are not to curse this people, for they are blessed." (Numbers 22:12) Then a bigger batch of princes showed up with a fancier offer, and Balaam asked God again anyway (Numbers 22:19).

Now look at the road. The angel of the LORD said, "I have come out to oppose you, because your way is perverse before me." (Numbers 22:32) Balaam was so locked on where he was headed that his own donkey saw what he couldn't. And I'll be honest, I've been so sure of myself I'd have argued with a talking donkey too. Wait, that's exactly what he did.

The good news is that God doesn't leave Balaam in the dark. The LORD opened the donkey's mouth, and the LORD opened Balaam's eyes (Numbers 22:28, 31). So when you catch yourself leaning toward what you want instead of what God has said, ask Him to open your eyes, and then listen when He answers. This story isn't over, friend, so keep your apron on.
